newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold finishes down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold finishes down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong's bullion market saw healthy two-way professional business on Thursday before ending down from New York's close on Wednesday, gold dealers and traders in the territory said.
Speculative gold selling from Japan on dollar/yen movements during morning trade pushed Hong Kong gold down to its intra-day low of $379.35/85, traders said.
Players on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) sell gold to obtain dollars, an advantageous move when the dollar strengthens against the yen.
The afternoon saw good buying interest from professionals locally and overseas, specifically from Swiss players, gold sources said.
Solid buying interest pushed gold up near $380 in brisk trade, with offers from Europe hovering between $379.50-379.80, sources said.
But producers were said staying clear of the market, waiting for gold to climb back to and beyond $380.
Physical gold demand simmered but no exceptional activity was seen, traders said, noting volumes were moderate.
"It's still a bit bearish and somewhat quiet," said one gold trader, noting that players were still putting off buy orders.
Bullion ended at US$379.40/379.90 an ounce Thursday against New York's US$379.75/380.25 close on Friday.
Local gold ended HK$1 lower at HK$3,494 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -6 on Thursday from -5 on Friday.
